criteria.definition: LOCKED CANON: compare every declared date/age, setting, premise, character ID, dialect, style, aspect, target edit duration and prior user approval with exact latest approved value. Contradiction => FAIL; uncertain continuity => NOT_VERIFIED.

SPEAKING & TOTAL DRAMATIC CHARACTER COUNTS: scan EVERY dialogue cue, speaker label, script line, V.O., O.S., offscreen call, phone/radio/recorded speech, personified narrator, flashback, non-dialogue named action role and credit against P1.0; list the distinct identities, not just on-screen faces. Fail unauthorized additions or missing count. Explicitly track actor=existing-role aliases. Zero substantive dialogue => FAIL dialogue-film scope.

DIALOGUE INFORMATION LEDGER: for EACH asserted knowledge, record who knows what, when, source and whether it was audibly/visually accessible; verify quotes against actual preceding spoken lines. A character must not claim "I didn't say X" when X was previously spoken. Distinguish suspicion, testimony, circumstantial evidence, proof and confirmation. Never promote a suspect into proven perpetrator/kill verdict by unverified dialogue.

INTERVAL ARITHMETIC & SPOKEN DURATION: use canonical numeric seconds and one non-overlapping ordered interval per beat; start_0=0; end_i=start_{i+1}; total=last_end; SUM(per-beat durations)=film target; per-beat duration=end-start. For each beat/line count its actual dialogue words under an explicit reproducible Arabic word tokenization policy, annotate speaking_rate_words_per_second as JUSTIFIED_ESTIMATE (do not hard-code 1.5–2.0 as universal), and compute speech_seconds=word_count/rate. Assign independent non-overlapping physical-action, pause, visual reveal and reaction budgets unless actual parallel performance is explicitly demonstrated with overlap fields. No double-counted overlapping time. Reject any beat where required seconds exceed allotted seconds. Exact durations are production targets until measured from final approved audio and edit.

PHYSICAL & PROP CONTINUITY: stage geography, character positions, body parts, hand identity, reach/path, contact and release, force response, wardrobe, lighting sources, glass/reflections, hero prop access/transfer, unfastening, and actual continuity ledger must agree with screenplay. Protect important props in both active and transient states; no teleports or inexplicable camera/physics.

CAUSALITY & EXTERNAL CLAIMS: Every climax/payoff needs setup and accessible cause in the visible/heard story; no magically fast external help, unsupported forensic certainty, legal guarantees, medical/technical/historical assertion without appropriate verification and cautious wording. Source-check niche empirical claims when relevant research tools exist; otherwise mark uncertainty, rewrite to non-assertive story claim, or block critical claim. KB references do NOT certify jurisdiction-specific law or historical device specs.

OPENING HOOK & ENDING: within the first ~5–8 seconds for short-form formats present a compelling visible/audible question, contradiction, conflict, or emotionally meaningful action, unless specifically approved narrative alternative. Climax must change the situation via earned character decision; explicit setup-to-payoff chain plus BOTH external conflict consequence and protagonist internal/emotional turn where applicable. No obligatory surprise, siren or heroic victory. A strong slow-burn can keep silence and ambiguity, but not merely assert inner feelings with no filmable evidence.

DIALOGUE-DRIVEN PERFORMANCE: every core exchange advances conflict, tactic, relationship or information; natural approved dialect, distinct voices, measured pauses and listener-owned moments. Silence encouraged when meaningful, but cannot turn the film into Purely Visual/Silent. No mechanically imposed talking density.

PRODUCTION FEASIBILITY: distinguish what is filmable via shot sequence from what requires unverified simultaneous microscale detail, unsupported text, audio sync, camera/hand physics or rare historical material accuracy; flag feasibility not fake guarantee.

CROSS-ARTIFACT CONSISTENCY: reconcile Story Bible, canonical screenplay, beat/scene timing, named lines, character registry, causal ledger, prop custody, dialogue packet and assessment report; no PASS if QA summary disagrees with actual text.
